author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  as a follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Specialty directory lists every specialty with the veterinarians holding it
summary: A read-only page publishes the veterinarian directory the other way round: every specialty the clinic knows, under its stored name, with the veterinarians holding it named in full. The whole list appears at once, and nothing in the interface links to the page.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows, each under its stored name.
Under each specialty, every veterinarian holding it is named by first name followed by last name, for example "Helen Leary".
A veterinarian holding no specialty is named nowhere on the page.
A veterinarian holding more than one specialty is named under each specialty held.
A specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, with no veterinarian named under it.
Every specialty appears on the one page, and the page carries no paging control.
No page of the interface links to the specialty directory, and no navigation entry leads to it.
Specialties, and the veterinarians under each, appear in a stable order across repeated requests.
Wording new to this page is externalized and present in every supported language, as REQ-LANG-002 requires of every page.
non_goals: creating, editing, or removing specialties or veterinarians — NG-2 is unchanged
a navigation entry, or any link from another page, leading to the specialty directory
searching or filtering the specialty listing — NG-9 is unchanged
a machine-readable form of the specialty listing — REQ-VET-002 was withdrawn 2026-07-31
paging the specialty listing, as the veterinarian directory pages its own
notes: PRD tag: I minted REQ-SPEC-001 in docs/prd.md for this slice; it corresponds to this log's req_id REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001, which does not follow the PRD's REQ-XX-NNN convention. Later records for this slice keep the log req_id so the thread stays one. No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. The address /specialties.html is quoted from the owner's request and is deliberately absent from the PRD, which states behavior only. Two open questions are recorded in the PRD rather than consulted, per the owner's instruction that no further product answer will come: whether the page should later gain a visible entry point, and which order the entries sort in — a stable order is required, the sort key is unstated. file_targets are best-effort; the template path is a guess for design to revise.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no module or dependency. Three things are new ground, which is why this is not `covered`: a repository for specialties (none exists), a non-persisted domain value object (the codebase has none), and a second HTML surface over vet data. The page cannot be answered from the veterinarian roster alone, because a specialty no veterinarian holds must still be listed. It is composed from a new `SpecialtyRepository` read plus the existing cached `VetRepository.findAll()`, grouped and ordered by a `SpecialtyDirectory` value object, and rendered by a new `SpecialtyController`. Grouping and ordering are domain rules with the PRD's own edge cases attached, so they may not sit in the controller: `architecture-principles.md` § Design Validation Checklist bars a new rule from a web controller, and `system-design.md` § Package Structure records the existing controller-rule deviation as not extending to new rules. Every new type matches an in-force catalog pattern (Repository, Value object, Web controller) and the naming rules. Recorded in `docs/system-design.md` § Contracts and ADR 2026-08-14-specialty-directory-derived-in-memory.
integration_points: GET /specialties.html is a new read-only route with no request parameter, no path variable, and no bound form type; it mutates nothing and needs no `@InitBinder`. It publishes specialty names and veterinarian names to every caller, which /vets.html and /vets already publish, so it widens no data exposure (security-principles.md § Realization, 'Widening the exposed surface').
`SpecialtyDirectory` reads `VetRepository.findAll()` — the `@Cacheable("vets")` overload — so the page shares the vet cache and adds no second read of the roster.
`SpecialtyRepository` is a new Spring Data interface over the existing `specialties` table; the schema, the seed data, and the JPA mapping are unchanged in all three vendor scripts.

The new template uses `fragments/layout` like every other page. The nav fragment gains no item, so the layout's menu argument should be a key matching no nav entry, leaving every entry inactive on this page (acceptance criterion 7).

Rendered wording is already in the bundles: `specialties`, `vets`, and `none`. New wording, if any is needed, goes into all eleven files under src/main/resources/messages/ or I18nPropertiesSyncTest fails.

patterns.description: precedent for a lookup-table repository read whole; the specialty repository mirrors it, except that ordering lives in SpecialtyDirectory rather than in the query
controller shape for a server-rendered vet page: read, populate the model, return a view name. The specialty page drops the pagination helper
template shape: layout fragment, a th:text heading from the bundle, a th:each table. Reuse it without the paging block
Pattern Catalog § In force — Value object, Repository, Web controller. The value object is the catalog's answer to a rule that may not enter the controller

risks.risk: BaseEntity defines neither equals nor hashCode, so a Specialty read through SpecialtyRepository is an unequal object to the same stored row reached through Vet.getSpecialties(). Grouping by object equality silently produces a directory in which no specialty has holders.
risks.mitigation: Match holders to specialties by persisted identity (getId()). Cover it with a directory test whose Vet carries a distinct Specialty instance with the same id and name.

risks.risk: The page inherits the vet cache, which has no eviction configured (system-design.md Open Question 5). Vet data changed out of band shows stale on this page exactly as it does on /vets.html.
risks.mitigation: Accept and inherit; add no new cache name, since CacheConfiguration declares only 'vets'. The exposure is unchanged from today's vet list.

risks.risk: A new type reached reflectively from a Thymeleaf expression can be missing reflection metadata in a GraalVM native image.
risks.mitigation: Make SpecialtyDirectory and its per-specialty entry public with public accessors. If the native build is exercised, register the type in PetClinicRuntimeHints alongside the existing Vet hint.

risks.risk: Passing 'vets' as the layout menu argument would light the Veterinarians nav entry while this page is open, blurring acceptance criterion 7.
risks.mitigation: Pass a menu key matching no nav item. Assert that no template links to /specialties.html.

risks.risk: A stable order is required (acceptance criterion 8) but is not in the given test_names, and the underlying reads carry no ORDER BY.
risks.mitigation: Order in SpecialtyDirectory: specialties by name, holders by last name then first name then id. Add a directory test that feeds the inputs in a shuffled order and asserts the output order.

notes: file_targets revised, as the prd-entry invited. VetController and VetRepository are NOT modified: the surface is a specialty page, and the owner package's precedent is one controller per domain noun (Owner/Pet/Visit), so SpecialtyController keeps VetController's dependencies and its @WebMvcTest slice untouched. The messages path in file_targets was src/main/resources/messages.properties; the bundles actually live in src/main/resources/messages/. Test placement for the given names: ListEverySpecialtyByStoredName, OmitAVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty, NameAVeterinarianUnderEachSpecialtyHeld, and ListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds are grouping rules and belong in SpecialtyDirectoryTests with real Vet and Specialty objects and no Spring context; NameHoldersByFirstThenLastName and ShowEverySpecialtyOnOnePage assert the rendered page and belong in SpecialtyControllerTests via MockMvc. Empty-clinic edge case (PRD edge case 3) renders an empty listing rather than failing — cover it in the directory test. The PRD's open ordering question is answered narrowly at design time by ADR 2026-08-14 (name order; the owner may revisit). The PRD uses 'holder' for a veterinarian holding a specialty; docs/ubiquitous-language.md carries no such term, and I did not add one — vocabulary is the product expert's to write. Consult me if the naming of the per-specialty entry type is unclear: it must be a domain noun with no prohibited suffix.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain: no NVD match ran in this review. build.gradle declares no OWASP dependency-check plugin (plugins are java, checkstyle, jacoco, spring-boot 4.1.0, dependency-management, graalvm native, cyclonedx, javaformat), so `./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze` is not available and the reviewer has no network access. Treat the dependency posture as NOT VERIFIED against the NVD for this pass. The risk is bounded here because the change set adds and modifies no dependency — build.gradle is untouched by the slice — so the resolved artifact set is identical to the pre-slice baseline. Closing the check is a CI or human task, not a blocker for this change.

Robustness note, not an attacker path: SpecialtyDirectory.holds() dereferences specialty.getId() unconditionally. Every specialty on this path comes from persistence and carries an id, and no request-supplied value reaches the comparison, so there is no reachable NPE from an attacker-controlled input. If the value object is ever reused with a transient Specialty, the guard becomes worth adding.
approved_aspects: No request-derived input anywhere in the slice: GET /specialties.html binds no path variable, request parameter, or form type, so the mass-assignment, path-traversal, and injection rows of security-principles.md § Realization have no surface to apply to. No @InitBinder is required because nothing is bound.

Data access stays on the repository abstraction: SpecialtyRepository declares only a derived findAll() over Spring Data, with no string-concatenated query text. It is read-only by construction (@Transactional(readOnly = true), Repository base interface with no write method), which is least privilege for the specialty lookup table.

Template output escaping stays on: src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html renders every dynamic value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, the holder name concatenation, and the #{none} message). No th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource reference, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) of any model value. Verified by grep for th:utext and __${ across src/main/resources/templates/ — the only preprocessing hits in the tree are vetList.html's pager over server-computed page integers, which this slice does not touch.

Escaping matches the neighboring implementation of the same concern (vetList.html renders vet and specialty names the identical way), so the Pattern Consistency check passes with no divergence to justify.

No widening of the exposed surface: the page publishes specialty names and veterinarian names, both already published by /vets.html and /vets. No management endpoint, no mutating route, and no new data class reaches a caller.

Native-image hints add reflection only: PetClinicRuntimeHints registers SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyDirectory.Entry with MemberCategory.INVOKE_PUBLIC_METHODS, not withJavaSerialization(true). The Java-serialization surface named in the threat model is unchanged, and no endpoint accepts serialized input.

Concurrency and state: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding two repository references; SpecialtyDirectory and its Entry are records that defensively copy their lists (List.copyOf) in the compact constructors, so the model object handed to the view is immutable and safe to share.

No secrets, credentials, or connection strings introduced: a case-insensitive scan of the full change set for password/secret/token/apikey/credential returns nothing. No shell execution (Runtime/ProcessBuilder), no unsafe Jackson configuration (enableDefaultTyping/@JsonTypeInfo), no file I/O, and no system /tmp use anywhere in the diff.
No new logging, so no log-injection or sensitive-data-in-logs surface; no exception message is constructed that could carry internal detail onto the error page.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply-chain NVD match did not run and is therefore not clean, only unverified: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, so ./gradlew dependencyCheckAnalyze does not exist and this reviewer has no network access. Every request-reachable path reads specialties from the store, so the id is non-null there and no attacker-reachable NPE exists; a transient Specialty constructed in a future test or caller would fail with an NPE whose message the error page renders. Consider matching on the holder side first or guarding the id, if the type is ever used off the persisted path.

IDE semantic oracle was not consulted (headless run), so the route-exposure conclusion above rests on reading the single new @GetMapping and the design doc's Contracts rows rather than on resolved-symbol references — the weaker basis, though the surface is one literal-mapped controller method.
approved_aspects: No new trust boundary: SpecialtyController.showSpecialtyDirectory(Model) binds no request-derived value at all — no @RequestParam, @PathVariable, or command object — so mass assignment, path traversal (the view name 'vets/specialtyList' is a literal), and cross-request-state rows of security-principles.md Realization are not reachable here.

Data access is a Spring Data derived query (SpecialtyRepository.findAll(), @Transactional(readOnly = true), no write method declared) with no string-concatenated query text — the injection-into-data-access row passes, and the read-only, read-whole interface matches least privilege.

Output escaping: specialtyList.html renders every derived value through th:text (entry.specialty.name, holder.firstName/lastName) with default escaping on; no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource, and no Thymeleaf preprocessing (__${...}__) of any value on this template — the XSS row passes and the escaping mechanism matches the neighboring vetList.html.

Native-image hints widen reflection minimally: SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyDirectory.Entry are registered with MemberCategory.INVOKE_PUBLIC_METHODS only, deliberately not withJavaSerialization as the three persisted types are — the unsafe-deserialization surface is not extended.

Exposed surface: GET /specialties.html is read-only and publishes only specialty names and veterinarian names, both already public via /vets.html; the route, its unpaged shape, and its components are documented in docs/system-design.md (Contracts rows) and REQ-SPEC-001, satisfying the 'a change that adds an endpoint states what it exposes and to whom' rule. No management endpoint exposure changed.

No secrets, credentials, or connection strings added anywhere in the diff (scanned production, template, and both test files for token/password/secret/key/credential); no logging added, so no log-injection or sensitive-log path.

No shell execution, file I/O, XML/YAML/JSON parsing, regex, or randomness introduced; the derived model is immutable (record with List.copyOf in both canonical constructors) and the controller holds no mutable singleton state, so the concurrency row passes.
